transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Evelyn Chen (Nimbus - Head of ML), Marcus Rivera (Nimbus - Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Nimbus - Security), Sam Ortiz (Nimbus - Data Eng)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in. Focus on environment readiness: network access, SSO/KMS, and running E2E benchmarks. Discussed preliminary latency numbers from quick smoke tests; agreed to run a fuller load test on staging. Action items and owner assignments at the end.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this tight, we've got about 45 minutes, quick agenda — onboarding, access, bench results, and next steps. daniel will cover the benchmark plan.
[00:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): cool, yeah hi all. quick status update from our side: we completed the model spin-up in our staging image, loaded the quantized 8-bit build for the model variant we discussed, ran a small smoke test, and saw ~45ms p50 and ~210ms p95 on single-request inference in our GPU dev instance. caveats apply, latency will change under batching.
[00:36] Evelyn (Nimbus): got it, thanks. when you say 210ms p95, is that for a 512-token request or shorter prompts? our baseline is usually 256 tokens.
[00:50] Daniel: ah yes, that was 256 tokens with a 2-token warm prefix; with the 128 token profile we see p95 closer to ~160ms. but again this was on a small test rig — the Dedicated pool numbers will vary.
[01:05] Marcus (Nimbus): quick context, our staging cluster is on GCP in us-west1 with a mix of T4s and A100s for other workloads. for this pilot we can provision an A10g node if needed, but we want to keep cost visible.
[01:22] Sofia: right, and we can recommend model/kernel mappings based on seq lengths — we'll include that in the tuning doc.
[01:30] Priya (Nimbus - Security): small but important — we haven't yet given Redwood access to our staging network. we need SSO integration and a VPN jump host per our security policy. also will want to understand KMS integration for any logs or artifacts that touch PII.
[01:48] Daniel: understoood. Priya, for SSO we support SAML SSO and can accept metadata; for the VPN/jump host we can do a temporary IP allowlist to validate. for KMS we can integrate with customer-managed keys for storage of any persisted artifacts — we have an HSM/KMS support doc. I'll share the doc after the call.
[02:10] Priya: ok, please include who on your side will have key access and what audit logs look like. we need to map that to our auditors.
[02:20] Daniel: sure, we'll include a table: roles, access, and audit retention.
[02:25] Sam (Nimbus): small note — the test prompts include both long technical docs and short search-like queries; we should validate both.
[02:35] Daniel: totally; our benchmark plan will include three profiles: short (<=64 tokens), medium (~256 tokens), and long (~512-1024 tokens). we'll measure p50, p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens approx.
[02:50] Sofia: can we talk about environment readiness specifically — Marcus, status of firewall and jump host?
[02:58] Marcus: firewall needs a rule; i opened an internal ticket earlier but haven't pushed the allowlist yet. i can add Redwood's staging IPs, but i need the exact CIDR ranges.
[03:10] Sofia: i'll send the list right after this meeting. also note that for Dedicated testing we can provide a temporary whitelist and then move to SSO once things look good.
[03:22] Evelyn: timeline wise, we want pilot results by mid-October so product can decide on roll-out. is that realistic?
[03:30] Daniel: yes, if we get network access and the prompt set this week we can run full E2E benchmarks early next week.
[03:40] Priya: regarding KMS and logs — do you store request logs by default? we need to understand retention and deletion options.
[03:50] Sofia: by default hosted logging captures request metadata but you can opt out of storing request bodies; for Private/Dedicated deployments you keep full control and logs can be routed to your KMS/HSM and logging stack. we'll send the SOC2/ISO compliance pack.
[04:05] Marcus: also curious about caching — you mentioned prefix/KV caching earlier. how does that interact with multi-tenant staging?
[04:15] Daniel: good question. the KV cache is per model instance and can be configured per-customer. for this pilot we can spin an isolated cache so your traffic doesn't collide with others. prefix caching will speed up repeat prefix-heavy queries.
[04:30] Sofia: ok here's the benchmark plan in bullets, daniel please confirm: 1) run short/med/long profiles, 2) measure p50/p95/throughput/cost, 3) run 10-minute steady-state load and 30-second burst tests, 4) produce a single-sheet result and a raw data CSV.
[04:50] Daniel: yep, that's it. we'll also test quantization variants (8-bit vs 16-bit FP) to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:00] Evelyn: do you have any early cost back-of-envelope for our expected usage? we're trying to compare hosted vs dedicated.
[05:08] Sofia: early ballpark: hosted is easier but per-token unit costs are higher; Dedicated has higher fixed cost but lower variable cost if you sustain throughput. we'll send example math based on your expected tokens/day once you share the workload estimate.
[05:22] Sam: sending the workload estimate today.
[05:25] Marcus: one more infra point — our staging uses internal auth to access model artifacts, any requirement there? we can provide read-only creds.
[05:35] Daniel: read-only creds to pull model artifacts are fine; for the cache and inference endpoints we'll need to validate network egress.
[05:45] [10-minute marker omitted for brevity]
[15:00] Daniel: jumping ahead to tuning recommendations — for medium prompts we saw the best tradeoff using A10g + 8-bit quantization with batch size 4; for long prompts you might prefer A100 and batch size 2 to avoid memory pressure.
[15:20] Evelyn: memory pressure — are there any OOM patterns we should watch for when sequence length varies widely?
[15:30] Daniel: yes variable sequence lengths can cause tail spikes; we typically recommend dynamic batching and a conservative max_seq config. also enable KV cache where repeats are common.
[15:45] Priya: regarding audit logs — what's retention and who can access? we need at least 12 months retention and audit entries tied to user identities.
[15:55] Sofia: that's standard for our Enterprise pack; retention and access controls can be configured via RBAC and integrated with your SIEM. we'll include a sample retention policy doc.
[16:05] Marcus: ok practical access steps now — Priya will send SSO metadata, Marcus will open firewall by end of day, Sam will drop the prompt set, and we wait for daniel's benchmark results.
[16:20] Daniel: one technical caveat — in our smoke test we saw a small mismatch in tokenization for a proprietary tokenizer snippet; some system tokens got split unexpectedly. it's likely a tokenizer config mismatch — please share the tokenizer config used by your ingestion pipeline.
[16:40] Sam: noted, will attach that to the prompt set.
[16:48] Evelyn: can we also get a short recording of the benchmark run or logs for debugging?
[16:55] Daniel: yes we can save and share logs; we'll redact any real data and provide synthetic traces where necessary.
[17:05] Sofia: competition question — have you evaluated Anthropic or OpenAI for this workload? any hard constraints steering you away?
[17:12] Evelyn: we've done initial evals with OpenAI for prototyping but security and cost are concerns; Anthropic had some quality on long-form but integration is heavier. pricing and regional hosting matter.
[17:25] Sofia: good to know. we'll highlight regional hosting and privacy controls in the follow-up.
[17:35] [Crosstalk — brief] Marcus: sorry one more infra Q — do you support private deployment in our VPC?
[17:42] Sofia: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in-customer VPC/on-prem with a private control plane; that's part of our enterprise offering. we'll include an architecture sketch.
[17:55] Priya: for Private deployments, do you provide HSM integrations and can we bring our own KMS?
[18:02] Daniel: yes you can bring your own KMS, we support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed stores for secrets. we'll add the integration steps.
[18:15] Sofia: ok let's recap actions and owners.
[18:20] Daniel: i'll run the benchmarks, collect p50/p95/throughput, and upload results.
[18:25] Marcus: i'll open the firewall and confirm CIDRs.
[18:28] Priya: i'll get SSO metadata and KMS contact info to you.
[18:32] Sofia: i'll share pricing, SOW template, and compliance docs.
[18:35] Evelyn: we'll provide the prompt set and tokenizer config, target by Friday.
[18:40] Sofia: excellent. any other blockers?
[18:45] Sam: none from data eng.
[18:48] Marcus: no.
[18:50] Sofia: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in Asana and email, next sync same time next week if needed.
[19:00] (meeting ends)

References/Artifacts mentioned:
- Benchmark plan (will be shared by Daniel)
- SOC2/ISO compliance pack (Sofia to send)
- Pilot SOW and pricing examples (Sofia to send)
- Prompt set and tokenizer config (Nimbus to share)
- Shared spreadsheet for benchmark results (Redwood SE to upload)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and minor transcription artifacts; speaker "Speaker 1" present from notes system.
